div.head: I Cn 26.1
div.ab: Forþam wace byð se hyrde funden to heorde, þe nele þa heorde, þe he healdan sceal, mid hreame bewerian, butan he elles mæge, gyf þær hwylc þeodsceaða sceaðian onginneð.
Forðam wace se hyrde bið funden to hyrde, ðe nele ða heorde, ðe he healdan scéal, mid hréame bewerian, buton [he] helles mǽge, gyf ðær hwylc ðeodsceaða sceaðian onginneð.
Forþam wac bið se hyrde funden to heorde, þe nele þa heorde, þe healdan sceal, mid hreame bewerian, buton he elles mæge, gyf ðær hwylc þeodsceaða sceaðian onginneð.
quia superuacue pastor est, qui commisso sibi gregi non uult saltem clamore succurrere, si quid ei noceat.
Debilis namque nimium custos ipse ad custodiam inuentus est, qui custodiam cui preest saltim ex preclamacione defendere non uult, nisi aliter queat, si quis latro latrocinari incipit.
Forðam wace se hyrde bi[ð] funden to hyrde ðe nele ða heorde ðe he healdan scéal mid hréame bewerian, buton he elles mǽge, gyf ðær hwylc ðeodsceaða sceaðian onginneð.
Forþam wace byð se hyrde funden to heorde þe nele þa heorde þe he healdan sceal, mid hreame bewerian, butan he elles mæge gyf þær hwylc þeodsceaða sceaðian onginneð.

Denn schwach wird jener Hirt für seine Herde befunden, der es unterlässt, die Herde, die er hüten soll — wenn er es auf andere [stärkere] Art nicht vermag —, durch Zuruf zu schützen, falls da irgend ein Volksschädiger [Erzfeind] zu schaden beginnt.

For that shepherd is found weak for his flock who will not defend the flock which he must keep — if he cannot do it in some other [stronger] way — by shouting, if any public enemy [the arch-enemy] begins to do harm there.

For a shepherd will be considered failing in his trust, if he will not provide for the safety of the flock, which is committed to his keeping, by raising the alarm, if he cannot do anything else, when any spoiler proceeds to harm it.
For the shepherd will be found wanting who will not cry out in defense of the flock entrusted to his care, if he can do nothing else when a predator comes to prey upon it.
div.note: ‘he’ supplied in A by Liebermann.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 307, October 2026 (MS Cons)

note.seg: Das Folgende bis 26, 3 Mitte wiederholt Polity c. 19 p. 432f. nochmals und 26, 1 bis Epilog der Homilet n. Wulfstan 191
What follows up to the middle of 26, 3 is repeated once again by Polity c. 19 p. 432f., and 26, 1 up to the epilogue by the Homilet n. Wulfstan 191

supervacue (s. Wb) Q ‘feige’, wohl nur Gleichklangs wegen.—Das Bild Hirt und Herde auch II 84, 2.—Vgl. das Sprichwort Ðonne se heretoga wacað, þonne bið eall se here swiðe gehindred; Ann. Agsax. 1003, wozu Plummer vergleicht: si dux timidus erit, quomodo salvabitur miles? Alcuin Epist., Mon. Alcu. p. 621

Q’s supervacue (see Wb) for ‘cowardly’, probably only because of the assonance.—The image of shepherd and flock also II 84, 2.—Cf. the proverb Ðonne se heretoga wacað, þonne bið eall se here swiðe gehindred; Ann. Agsax. 1003, with which Plummer compares: si dux timidus erit, quomodo salvabitur miles? Alcuin Epist., Mon. Alcu. p. 621
Cons. wählt unter den Bedd. falsch ‘Hut’
Of the meanings, Cons. wrongly chooses ‘guard’
Nicht ‘wenn er anders kann’; der Homilet setzt huru (‘wenigstens’) statt des Satzes
Not ‘if he is otherwise able’; the homilist puts huru (‘at least’) in place of the clause

Nicht ‘Schaden’ (so Q, auch 26, 3. II 4, 2), noch ‘public robber’ (Thorpe); besonders der ‘Teufel’ (s. d. Gl 6) heisst leodscaða, wulf schon bei Cynewulf, sonst auch von Menschen (wie u. II 4, 2), Drachen, Hungersnot gesagt (Grein); þeodscaða dafür Hom. n. Wulfstan 80.—Episcopi praedicent .., ne aliquis per incuriam pastoris lupinis pateat morsibus lacerandus; Constit. Odonis Cant. a. 943, c. 3

Not ‘harm’ (so Q, also 26, 3. II 4, 2), nor ‘public robber’ (Thorpe); the ‘devil’ (see that word in Gl 6) in particular is called leodscaða, wulf as early as Cynewulf; the word is otherwise also used of men (as below II 4, 2), dragons and famine (Grein); þeodscaða instead in Hom. n. Wulfstan 80.—Episcopi praedicent .., ne aliquis per incuriam pastoris lupinis pateat morsibus lacerandus; Constit. Odonis Cant. a. 943, c. 3
With what follows to the middle of § 3, cf. Insts. of Polity, 19, ed. Thorpe, ii. p. 326. From § 1 to the end, cf. Wulfstan, p. 191.
The same metaphor is used in II Cn. 84, 2.
